clues.text: A bandleader who played this instrument collaborated with Juan Tizol on the Latin-flavored “Caravan.”
This instrument was played by the composer of "Watermelon Man", Herbie Hancock.
This instrument was named for its ability to play both loud and soft.
Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag is played on this instrument.
Dominico Scarlatti wrote 555 sonatas as one of the earliest composers for this instrument.
Among its most famous players are Thelonious Monk and Franz Liszt.
With Billy Strayhorn, a player of this instrument wrote “In a Sentimental Mood” and “Take The A Train.”
The blind Stevie Wonder notably played this instrument, whose three foot-operated pedals are oft-used in jazz.
Name this instrument played by Tommy Flannigan, Dave Brubeck, and Duke Ellington.
Name this keyboard instrument which has 88 black and white keys.
This movement emerged after an "Anonymous Society" organized an independent exhibition after being rejected from the Salon.
An American art collective known as The Ten was primarily associated with this art movement.
An American artist from this movement depicted a puppy and a bored child in a white dress lying in blue armchairs.
Alfred Sisley was a prominent English member of this movement who pioneered the usage of en plein air landscapes among its members.
The Child's Bath was a painting by an American member of this art movement, Mary Cassatt.
One member of this school painted the Houses of Parliament under varying weather conditions and another painted Van Gogh leaning over a boat rail in The Luncheon of the Boating Party.
One artist from this movement often painted his wife Camille Doncieux, and another member of it painted a boy poking his feet in a bowl of water in The Child's Bath.
A pioneer of this art movement portrayed haystacks throughout the seasons as well as a series of over 250 murals of water lilies.
Name this late 19th century art movement led by Mary Cassatt, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, and Claude Monet.
Auguste Renoir and Claude Monet were of what school of art?

answerlines: Sergei Rachmaninoff [or Sergei Vasilyevich Rachmaninoff] (The third clue refers to Isle of the Dead.)

clues.text: In the slow third movement of this composer’s second symphony, violins introduce the yearning motif “G-sharp, A, F-sharp” over the IV (“four”) chord, D major.
The fifth movement of this composer’s All-Night Vigil was sung at his funeral.
A long clarinet solo introduces the second theme of the Adagio from this composer’s Symphony No. 2 in E minor.
This composer’s first symphony, which extensively quotes the Dies Irae, had a disastrous premiere conducted by Alexander Glazunov.

One of his orchestral works based on gypsy themes ends in a loud E major chord, and alongside Caprice Bohemien, he wrote a suite with movements marked "Non allegro" and "Andante con moto" which uses a three-note motif and features alto saxophone near the beginning.
In a piece by this composer, the A minor main theme is inverted to D-flat major in its 18th variation.
He used a recurring motif in 5/8 time to suggest the movement of water in a symphonic poem based on a Böcklin painting, The Isle of the Dead.
The soloist alternates between bell-like chords and a low F to open this composer’s C minor second piano concerto, which he dedicated to his therapist Nikolai Dahl.
While living in exile in Switzerland, he composed a series of variations on the 24th Caprice of an Italian violin virtuoso.
Name this large-handed Russian pianist and composer of Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini.
